messages:
maria (ML): Heads-up — customer 'Siren' LoRA merge (v2) pushed to staging. Quick smoke shows a noticeable quality shift after int4 quantization. Can someone run the quick-eval pack + tokenizer sanity? @sameer @joey

sameer: On it. Which base checkpoint and merge args did you use?

maria (ML): Base: siren-base-3b, LoRA: customer/siren-lora-v2. Merge was a straightforward add_weights, no re-tokenization. Command I ran:
```
python tools/merge_lora.py --base siren-base-3b --lora customer/siren-lora-v2 --out merged/siren-v2 --preserve-tokenizer
python quantize.py --model merged/siren-v2 --format int4-triton
```
Quick eval (small sample):
- ppl: base_fp16=12.1, merged_fp16=11.9, merged_int4=14.3
- chrF: base_fp16=0.62, merged_fp16=0.63, merged_int4=0.57

joey: Hmm that ppl jump looks concentrated in convo prompts. Also saw weird token splits around contractions and emoji in a few examples. sample: "I can't believe it 😅" tokenized to: ["I", "can", "'", "t", "believe", "it", "▁😅"] — apostrophe split is odd.

eva: I'll run the tokenizer remap check against the LoRA vocab patch. Could be that the LoRA included tokenizer metadata that wasn't applied during merge. Running a token-diff: `python tools/token_diff.py --base siren-base-3b --lora customer/siren-lora-v2`

infra-bot: Deploy started: staging-gpu-3 -> merged/siren-v2 (quant=int4-triton). Logs: deploying container, loading KV cache, initializing Triton kernels. ETA ~4m.

qa-bot: Quick-eval pack finished (500 prompts). Summary:
- regressions concentrated in short, colloquial chat prompts (turns with emojis, contractions, and code snippets).
- top failure examples attached to the test run (run_id: run_2026_03_18_2212).
- suggestion: run one eval with fp16 merged model to confirm quantization is the main factor.

sameer: Reproduced locally. If I force the int4 kernel to use per-channel rounding_disabled the ppl drop to ~12.8 (still higher than fp16 but much closer). Suspecting a rounding/scale mismatch in the Triton int4 kernel or our quant config.

maria (ML): Good repro. For now let's fallback to merged_fp16 in staging and trigger a canary on dedicated. Also open a bug with triton-kernels: include the sample inputs that fail.

joey: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/siren/pull/432 — adds tokenizer regression tests and a tiny eval harness to reproduce the apostrophe/emoji splits. Running CI.

eva: Token diff shows the LoRA package included a small patch to tokenizer.json (added 24 special tokens). Merge step didn't always update merges.txt ordering when preserve-tokenizer flag used — I'll push a hotfix to merge tool to always canonicalize tokenizer after merge.

infra-bot: Staging updated: rolled back merged/siren-v2 (int4) -> merged/siren-v2 (fp16). Canary route set to 10%.

maria (ML): Thanks all. Action items: @sameer triage Triton kernel/biasing, @eva patch merge tool + add tokenizer canonicalization, @joey verify PR tests cover failing examples, @qa-bot run a 2k-prompt regression before next staging push. I'll inform the customer about temporary fp16 fallback.

sameer: Copy that — I'll include a minimal repro and open a kernel issue.

joey: CI passed for PR-432, tests include the 6 failing samples.

maria (ML): :thumbsup: keeping this thread as the coordination log. Follow-ups in the PR and kernel ticket.
